script_nghe: A few details about the project. We’ll be working in the Esk valley, in the north. It runs for six weeks. The main task is planting willow along the riverbanks — we had planned oak, but the ground turned out to be too wet. Accommodation is a shared cabin, basic but warm. You must bring waterproof boots; everything else is provided. And we leave at six thirty am, so please don’t be late.

> **Rewilding and its critics**
> 
> Rewilding — the practice of allowing land to return to a less managed state, sometimes assisted by reintroducing species that once lived there — has moved in twenty years from the margins of conservation to something close to orthodoxy. Faced with declining biodiversity and the high cost of intensive habitat management, several European governments have funded large-scale projects.
> 
> Supporters point to results achieved at surprisingly low cost. Having removed drainage systems and allowed grazing by hardy cattle, one Dutch reserve recorded increases in bird species that decades of careful management had failed to produce. Similar outcomes, though on a smaller scale, have been reported in Britain and Portugal.
> 
> Opposition has come from two directions. Farmers argue that land taken out of production must be replaced elsewhere, often in countries with weaker environmental standards — a criticism supporters find difficult to answer. Meanwhile some ecologists question the underlying idea. Landscapes described as natural, they point out, were shaped by human activity for thousands of years; choosing which past state to restore is a value judgement presented as a scientific one.
> 
> A further difficulty is time. Ecosystems recovering from intensive use may take a century to stabilise, while funding is typically committed for five years. Projects abandoned halfway can leave land in a condition worse than either the farmed or the restored state.

writing.bai_mau:
CÂU 1 — Because it lacked long-term funding, the project was abandoned.
  → Lacking long-term funding, the project was abandoned.
     [bỏ Because + chủ ngữ, đổi động từ sang V-ing]

CÂU 2 — After they had reviewed the data, the researchers changed their conclusion.
  → Having reviewed the data, the researchers changed their conclusion.
     [bỏ After + chủ ngữ, dùng Having + V3 vì hành động xảy ra trước]

CÂU 3 — The report which was submitted last week contains several errors.
  → The report submitted last week contains several errors.
     [bỏ which was, giữ V3 — rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ bị động]

BA CÂU BỔ SUNG để luyện thêm:
  · Being unable to attend, she sent a colleague.  [Because she was unable → Being]
  · Written in plain language, the guide is easy to follow.  [Because it is written → Written]
  · Faced with rising costs, many firms reduced their staff.  [Because they were faced → Faced]

cham_diem.vi_sao: Câu 1 dùng V-ing cho nguyên nhân cùng thời điểm. Câu 2 dùng Having + V3 vì hành động xảy ra trước hành động chính. Câu 3 rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ bị động, chỉ giữ V3.

cham_diem.tieu_chi: Chủ ngữ hai mệnh đề giống nhau (1đ)
cham_diem.vi_sao: Cả ba câu đều có chủ ngữ hai mệnh đề trùng nhau — điều kiện bắt buộc để rút gọn. Nếu khác nhau thì rút gọn sẽ tạo câu sai nghĩa.

dang_hoc:
Ba dạng rút gọn:
1. V-ing — hành động cùng lúc hoặc nguyên nhân: "Lacking funding, the project failed"
2. Having + V3 — hành động xảy ra trước: "Having finished, I left"
3. V3 — bị động: "The report submitted last week…"
ĐIỀU KIỆN BẮT BUỘC: chủ ngữ hai mệnh đề phải giống nhau. Khác nhau thì không rút gọn được.
Rút gọn làm câu ngắn hơn và học thuật hơn, rất phù hợp Writing Task 2.
Dùng 2–3 lần mỗi bài. Nhiều hơn thì câu nào cũng bắt đầu bằng V-ing, đọc rất nặng.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Lỗi nguy hiểm nhất: "Walking down the street, the building looked old." → chủ ngữ khác nhau nên thành ra toà nhà đang đi bộ. Phải viết: "Walking down the street, I thought the building looked old."
❌ Having finish the work → ✅ Having finished the work (phải là V3)
❌ The report submitting last week → ✅ The report submitted last week (bị động dùng V3)
❌ Bắt đầu 5 câu liền bằng V-ing → đọc rất đơn điệu.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 2 (2 phút) — Describe a difficult decision you made. Dùng mệnh đề rút gọn khi kể.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Part 2 — Describe a difficult decision you made (2 phút)
cau_tra_loi.mau:
I'd like to talk about my decision to go back to study after ten years of working.

Having worked in e-commerce since graduating, I'd reached a point where I was doing the same things repeatedly. Feeling that I was no longer developing, I started looking at master's programmes.

The decision was genuinely difficult. Faced with a hundred million dong in fees and roughly seven hundred hours of study, I hesitated for over a year. Being the only earner in my household made it harder still.

What finally convinced me was a conversation with my manager. Having seen several colleagues promoted into roles I wanted, I realised the gap wasn't technical skill — it was the language of management, which I'd never been taught.

Looking back, I'm glad I decided as I did, although I wish I'd started earlier. Committed now to a fixed schedule, I'm finding it more manageable than I feared.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Sáu mệnh đề rút gọn trong một bài nói tự nhiên: Having worked · Feeling that · Faced with · Being · Having seen · Looking back · Committed now. Dàn ý: bối cảnh → khó khăn → điều thuyết phục → nhìn lại.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Part 3 — Do people regret big decisions?
cau_tra_loi.mau: Some do, though in my experience regret comes more from decisions never made. Having spoken to older colleagues, I've noticed they rarely regret trying something — they regret waiting.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "Having spoken to…" trong lời nói hoàn toàn tự nhiên. Câu cuối đối lập ngắn gọn, rất mạnh.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Part 2 nói liền 2 phút, mệnh đề rút gọn giúp câu chuyển mượt.
repeatedly · hesitated · the only earner · manageable · genuinely.
Sáu mệnh đề rút gọn khác dạng · cấu trúc nhấn mạnh (What finally convinced me was…) · wish + quá khứ hoàn thành (I wish I'd started earlier).

meo_noi: Mệnh đề rút gọn nghe rất tự nhiên khi kể chuyện — đừng nghĩ nó chỉ dùng trong văn viết.
"Having + V3" mở đầu câu là cách gọn nhất để nối hai sự việc theo trình tự thời gian.
Dàn ý Part 2 cho đề "difficult decision": bối cảnh → hai khó khăn cụ thể → điều thuyết phục → nhìn lại.
